question:
Since version 1.5, dbt can be invoked directly from within a python script, like:

from dbt.cli.main import dbtRunner, dbtRunnerResult

# initialize
dbt = dbtRunner()

# create CLI args as a list of strings
cli_args = ["run-operation", "get_something_macro"]

# run the command
res: dbtRunnerResult = dbt.invoke(cli_args)

# inspect the results
for r in res.result:
    print(f"{r}")

See: https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/programmatic-invocations

Lets say I have a simple macro that returns something for example:

{% macro get_current_catalog() %}

    {{ return(target.catalog) }}

{% endmacro %}

How do I get the return value into python?

My only idea so far is using print("...") or log("...", info=True) within the macro and capture stdout. But I thought there has to be a better way...

Maybe some of you guys / gals know.
title: dbt - pass return value of dbt macro to python
answer:
Create a UDF instead of the jinja macro that does the logic for get_current_catalog() and call it as a sql query in the python model:

query = "SELECT get_current_catalog() AS CURRENT_CATALOG"
result = session.sql(query).to_pandas()
